# Story 1.1: Enrol an authenticator app
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an account holder, I want to enrol an authenticator app by scanning a QR code and confirming one code, so that my account has a second factor.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given a signed-in user without 2FA, when they start enrolment, then the page shows a QR code that encodes a newly generated TOTP secret.
- AC-2: Given a pending enrolment, when they submit the code currently shown by their authenticator app for that secret, then enrolment completes and 2FA is enabled on the account.
- AC-3: Given a pending enrolment, when they submit an incorrect code, then enrolment is not completed, 2FA stays disabled, and they see an error.
- AC-4: Given a pending enrolment that has not been confirmed, when the user signs in with their password, then they are signed in without being asked for a TOTP code.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Add the `totp_secret` column to the users table with a migration (AC: 1, 4)
- [ ] Generate a TOTP secret with pyotp and render a QR code for its provisioning URI on the enrolment page (AC: 1)
- [ ] Verify the submitted code against the pending secret with pyotp and mark enrolment complete on success (AC: 2, 3)
- [ ] Keep the secret in a pending state until confirmation so unconfirmed enrolment does not affect sign-in (AC: 4)

## Dev Notes
- FR-1 is the requirement behind this story.
- Architecture: TOTP verification uses pyotp and no new service is added; the secret is stored in the new `totp_secret` column on the existing Flask app's users table.

### References
- [Source: docs/prd.md#FR-1]
- [Source: docs/architecture.md#data-model]
- [Source: docs/architecture.md#verification]

# Story 1.2: Require a TOTP code at sign-in
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an account holder with 2FA enabled, I want to be asked for a current authenticator code after my password, so that a stolen password alone cannot sign me in.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given a user with 2FA enabled, when they submit a correct password, then they see a prompt for a TOTP code and are not yet signed in.
- AC-2: Given the TOTP prompt, when they submit the valid current code, then they are signed in.
- AC-3: Given the TOTP prompt, when they submit an invalid code, then they are not signed in and see an error.
- AC-4: Given a user without 2FA, when they submit a correct password, then they are signed in with no TOTP prompt.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] After a successful password check, redirect users with 2FA enabled to a TOTP step instead of creating the session (AC: 1, 4)
- [ ] Verify the submitted code against the user's `totp_secret` with pyotp (AC: 2, 3)
- [ ] Create the signed-in session cookie only after the TOTP step passes (AC: 2, 3)

## Dev Notes
- FR-2 is the requirement behind this story.
- Architecture: the existing session-cookie login is kept, so the session must not be set until the second factor passes; TOTP verification uses pyotp.

### References
- [Source: docs/prd.md#FR-2]
- [Source: docs/architecture.md#verification]

# Story 1.3: Recovery codes
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an account holder, I want ten single-use recovery codes issued when I enrol, so that I can still sign in if I lose my authenticator device.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given a user who has just completed enrolment, when enrolment is confirmed, then the page shows ten recovery codes.
- AC-2: Given the TOTP prompt, when the user submits an unused recovery code in place of a TOTP code, then they are signed in.
- AC-3: Given the TOTP prompt, when the user submits a recovery code that has already been used, then they are not signed in and see an error.
- AC-4: Given a user who has used one recovery code, when they sign in with a different unused recovery code, then sign-in succeeds, showing the other codes still work.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Add the `recovery_codes` column to the users table with a migration (AC: 1, 2, 3, 4)
- [ ] Generate ten recovery codes when enrolment is confirmed and show them on the confirmation page (AC: 1)
- [ ] Accept an unused recovery code at the TOTP step as an alternative to a TOTP code and mark it used (AC: 2, 4)
- [ ] Reject a recovery code that has already been used at the TOTP step (AC: 3)

## Dev Notes
- FR-3 is the requirement behind this story.
- Architecture: recovery codes live in the new `recovery_codes` column on the existing users table; the code is consumed on use, so the TOTP step must update that column as part of a successful sign-in.

- [Source: docs/prd.md#FR-3]
- [Source: docs/architecture.md#data-model]
- [Source: docs/architecture.md#verification]

- [ ] Verify the submitted code with pyotp against `totp_secret` (AC: 2, 3)

# Story 1.2: Custom per-key limit overrides the default
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an integration partner, I want my API key to carry a custom limit, so that my existing burst traffic keeps working unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given an API key with a custom limit above the default, when it sends requests beyond the default but within the custom limit, then those requests are served and not rejected with 429.
- AC-2: Given an API key with a custom limit, when it exceeds that custom limit in the window, then the response is 429 with a Retry-After header.
- AC-3: Given an API key with no custom limit, when it exceeds the default limit, then the response is 429 with a Retry-After header.
- AC-4: Given the two existing integration partners' keys, when they send their current traffic, then none of their requests are rejected with 429.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Add a nullable limit column to the `api_keys` table; null means "use the default" (AC: 1, 2, 3, 4)
- [ ] Read the key's limit at request time and fall back to the default when the column is null (AC: 1, 2, 3)
- [ ] Set custom limits on the two existing integration partners' keys so their current traffic fits within them (AC: 4)
- [ ] Apply the custom limit when deciding 429 and Retry-After, using the same counter as the default path (AC: 2, 3)

## Dev Notes
- FR-2 is the requirement behind this story.
- Architecture: limits are per API key and read from the existing `api_keys` table, which has no limit column yet, so the column is added here (data-model). The counter stays in Redis (counter-store).

# Story 1.3: Rate-limit counters survive an application restart
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an API operator, I want rate-limit counters to survive an application restart, so that restarting the service does not hand every client a fresh budget.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given an API key that has made N requests in the current window, when the application restarts, then the count for that key still reflects N.
- AC-2: Given an API key that exhausted its limit before a restart, when it sends a request after the restart, then the response is 429 with a Retry-After header.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Hold all counter state in Redis only, with no copy in application memory that a restart would discard (AC: 1, 2)
- [ ] Verify across a restart that counts continue from their pre-restart values (AC: 1)
- [ ] Verify across a restart that an exhausted key is still rejected with 429 (AC: 2)

## Dev Notes
- CAP-1 is the requirement behind this story.
- Architecture: Redis is the intended counter store (counter-store), so counters live outside the application process and outlive it.
